patch_description: Builds on the previous "parity-shared" ansatz by pushing parameter economy further while enriching the entangling structure through *multi-scale* weight sharing rather than more distinct angles. Instead of splitting rotations into even/odd families (2 rotation params) and a single nearest-neighbor entangling ring (1 param) — 5 distinct trainable circuit angles — this design uses only **3 distinct circuit parameters total**: one global RY angle applied to every qubit, one global RZ angle applied to every qubit, and one global entangling angle reused across three different entangling "shells" (nearest-neighbor distance-1 ring, distance-2 skip ring, and distance-4 long-range pairing). This mirrors a convolutional-style weight-sharing inductive bias (translation invariance across scales) known to help generalization from few examples in classical ML, while giving the ansatz genuinely global connectivity (every qubit pair is within reach through some combination of shells) instead of only nearest-neighbor coupling. Because the block is repeated 3 times with tied parameters, the effective circuit still reaches meaningful depth and expressivity despite the extreme parameter economy (3 circuit params + gain/bias = 5 total, down from 7), which the scoring rule rewards directly, while the richer multi-scale entangling pattern is intended to produce more robust cross-qubit correlations that generalize better to the hardest validation group than a single nearest-neighbor ring.
